rows.result: lintegral gives nonnegative ratio moments without erasing infinity; rpow supplies the real rho power on nonnegative well-defined ratios and exp supplies the deterministic bounds. These functions do not establish either quasi-likelihood inequality.
rows.gap: Define the forward and inverse quasi-likelihood ratios on a justified domain and prove both uniform moment bounds under the true sampling law.

comparisons.D46: Preserve the forward ratio p^natural(lambda,Y)/p^natural(lambda-star,Y) and the inverse ratio raised to rho>0 as distinct expectations, with negative c1 and positive c2 exponents respectively. Both are taken under P_lambda-star^(n), not a normalized quasi-likelihood law. Assumption E fixes absolute positive constants before all truths in Lambda_n-star, models and sufficiently large n; E1 further ranges over all lambda in Lambda_n. Nonnegative likelihood alone does not specify ratios at zero denominators; real division by zero and rpow extensions cannot settle this. Measurable nonnegative ratios can be coerced to ENNReal and integrated while retaining infinite moments, but their finite exponential bounds require proof.

rows.result: klDiv gives the nonnegative extended prior divergence and lintegral gives the expected n-times-squared discrepancy under a supplied variational witness. No inspected result constructs that witness or gives its uniform budget.
rows.gap: Construct an admissible variational witness satisfying the uniform KL-plus-squared-discrepancy budget under Assumption E2.

comparisons.D47: Keep the existential Q-star_n,m in Q_n,m, KL(Q-star_n,m,Pi_n,m), and the second term integrated over theta under that same Q-star, namely n*d_n(T(theta),lambda-star)^2. This term is not a KL divergence between sampling distributions as in A2. With measurable discrepancy, use lintegral of its nonnegative ENNReal value and add klDiv before comparing to the finite c3*n*(eta+zeta)^2 bound. The witness may vary with truth/model/n; the absolute constants and sufficiently-large-n scope must remain outside those choices. Retain the Assumption E truth class Lambda_n-star and the recorded discrepancy with the theorem’s broader printed class.

rows.result: IsLittleO and IsBigO express the two sequence-rate restrictions at atTop, with norm comparisons agreeing with the nonnegative log expressions on the positive dimension/sample domain. They do not encode the separate index inequalities automatically.
rows.gap: Bundle the source rate restrictions and model-index bounds with their exact asymptotic scope for Theorem 5.3.

comparisons.D40: Encode s_n*r_n*log(d_n)=o(n) and log(n)=O(log(d_n)), preserving the direction of log d_n ≳ log n. Also require s_n≥r_n and M_n=[m_max,n] with r_n≤m_max,n≤n, rather than using an arbitrary model subset. On natural positive dimensions the usual log is appropriate; do not rely on Real.log 0=0. This excerpt imports assumptions only: it does not import Theorem 5.2’s contraction conclusion as a premise or add the stronger signal conditions from (5.12).

rows.result: The row support and its finite cardinality express the sparsity constraint; singularValues applied to the Euclidean linear operator of L L-transpose gives the largest signal singular value, indexed zero in Lean. PosDef expresses the covariance codomain.
rows.gap: Define the true covariance class through admissible loading witnesses and prove the matrix-to-operator and sparsity correspondences.

comparisons.D38: The class consists of covariance images T(L)=L L-transpose+I with L having r_n columns, at most s_n nonzero rows, and sigma_1(L L-transpose)≤bar-sigma. Apply singularValues to L L-transpose, not to L or the covariance including I, and translate paper index 1 to library index 0. Set.encard of Function.support L is finite on row indices. Retain s_n≥r_n and bar-sigma>0; no full column rank, exact row count, or positive minimum signal is imposed here. Membership is existence of a loading representation satisfying these bounds, not a chosen identifiable loading matrix.

rows.result: singularValues supplies the ordered signal values, EuclideanSpace.norm_eq supplies each squared row length, and min-prime computes the minimum of the finite row-value set when nonempty. They do not package the restricted covariance class or prove selection consistency.
rows.gap: Construct the restricted true covariance class with both signal lower bounds and justify the active-row minimum’s nonempty domain.

comparisons.D39: Equation (5.12) bounds below both sigma_r_n(L L-transpose) and the minimum squared Euclidean norm over active rows by eta-star>0. Translate r_n to library index r_n-1 with the positive index proof and use the operator of L L-transpose; do not substitute sigma_r_n(L) or the covariance eigenvalue shifted by one. Preserve membership in the basic true class and the same loading representation. Finset.min-prime requires nonempty active support, so no empty-set real minimum may be invented; any equivalent universal row bound needs the appropriate domain justification. These extra signal conditions enter Theorem 5.3 and are not assumptions of Theorem 5.2.
